title: Where the planets are ten and twenty years later
question: From the positions and velocities of the Sun, the planets and the Moon on 2000-01-01 (given in inputs.json), predict where Mercury, Mars and Jupiter are seen from the Sun at later dates: their heliocentric ecliptic longitude, in degrees.

conditions.inputs: inputs.json: barycentric state vectors and GM values of the Sun, Mercury, Venus, the Earth, the Moon, and the barycentres of the Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto systems, 2000-01-01 00:00 TDB
conditions.frame: ecliptic and mean equinox of J2000; longitude measured from the x axis of that frame, counter-clockwise about its z axis, of the planet's position minus the Sun's
conditions.what_is_measured: positions of the planets as determined from decades of optical, radar and spacecraft observations; the answer is the position in the Solar System on that date, not a model's

practice.note: from the same source as the hidden cases; public so that an entrant can check frames and dates
